The largest size a texture keeps, by type. The type comes from the file name, e.g. ironsword_n.dds is a Normal map.

A .dds texture carries smaller copies of itself, each half the size of the one above. The plugin skips the largest ones and hands the game the first that fits your limit. Nothing is resampled and no file on disk is changed.
A limit applies to the longer side: a 4096x2048 texture capped at 1024 loads at 1024x512.
Changes apply to textures loaded from then on. A texture already in memory keeps its size until the game loads it again.
Textures without smaller copies, cubemaps, texture arrays and render targets are never touched.
The type comes from the end of the file name, see Categories. A texture whose name can't be read counts as Diffuse.
A rule matches anywhere in the path, file name included, and wins over the type limit. Case and slash direction don't matter. Full size leaves matching textures untouched.
Close a rule on both sides or it catches more than you meant: sky also matches actors\character\facegendata\facetint\skyrim.esm, \sky\ does not.
Give a rule a type and it only covers that type. Rules are checked from the top and the first match wins, so the narrow rule goes above the broad one:
That caps character normal maps at 2048 and leaves the rest of the folder alone. Swap them and the Normal rule never applies.
Lists every folder under Data\textures, plus the ones the base game keeps in its archives.
Loose files: .dds files sitting directly in that folder. A dash means there are none: the folder only holds subfolders, or only exists in an archive.
Used: how many textures the game loaded from that folder while tracking was on. A texture loaded twice counts twice. Tracking costs a little on every texture load, so it is off by default.
Folders packed in a mod's own archive only appear once tracking has seen one of their textures load.

Reduce above VRAM, on the General page, keeps textures at full size until video memory usage reaches that share of the budget. Usage is checked a few times a second, and textures go back to full size once it drops 5% below the threshold.
It doesn't shrink textures already loaded. It stops usage from climbing further, and memory comes back as the game unloads textures, for example when you change area.
Changes made in this menu apply at once. Save writes them to Data\SKSE\Plugins\TextureDownscaler.ini. Reload drops unsaved changes and reads the file again.
With Log level at Debug, TextureDownscaler.log gets a line for every texture loaded at a reduced size, with its name and type. The log sits in the SKSE folder under Documents\My Games.
